milestones.name: Foundations and launch
milestones.goal: Get the game as it stands onto a public URL, so every later change ships somewhere real.

tasks.description: Create the public GitHub repository and push the existing history
Deploy the current client-side game to Vercel from the repository

milestones.name: Design spikes
milestones.goal: Answer the open design questions before building on assumptions that may not survive them.

tasks.description: Gameplay-loop spike: interrogate the core premise, victory conditions, action economy and pacing, evaluate the six existing mechanics (Hold, Reform, Teach, Consolidate, Daughter band, Migrate), and define how condition, strain and action-budget states are derived
tasks.notes: Everything is open, including whether eight eras of three actions ending in a reconstruction is the right shape at all. Output is a design decision plus new tasks for whatever it finds wanting.

tasks.description: UI spike: information architecture first, then visual design; defines how the derived states are displayed, and produces concrete mobile and accessibility tasks rather than principles
tasks.notes: Absorbs the former standalone mobile and accessibility objectives. Gated on state derivation because it cannot design the display of states whose derivation is unsettled. The canvas map currently has no keyboard or screen-reader path; that gap must leave this spike as real tasks.

milestones.name: Persistence
milestones.goal: Runs survive the session and finished runs are comparable, attributed to a signed-in player.

tasks.description: Build the MongoDB data layer: runs and scores collections with their document shapes and access helpers
tasks.notes: Document shapes are already declared as RunDocument and ScoreDocument in src/lib/types.ts; the driver and adapter are installed.

tasks.description: Wire Auth.js with a GitHub OAuth app and enforce document ownership in the server routes
tasks.notes: Depends on the deploy for the live callback URL. MongoDB has no row-level security, so ownership checks live in the SvelteKit server routes rather than the database.

tasks.description: Save and resume a run across sessions and devices
tasks.notes: The serialised state shape needs a schema version: GameState will keep changing through the simulation-depth milestone, and old saved runs must not break on load.

tasks.description: Leaderboard of finished runs
tasks.notes: Deliberately not a first-class feature; a small indexed collection is enough.

milestones.name: Simulation depth
milestones.goal: Deepen the drift model and inter-culture dynamics so reconstruction has something harder to work on.

tasks.description: Derive a narrative condition state, replacing numeric prosperity entirely
tasks.notes: No float, no bar. Prosperity currently drives death at zero and the daughter-band threshold, so the derivation must preserve those mechanics while the player only ever sees prose.

tasks.description: Derive a narrative strain state, replacing the count of straining parts
Derive a narrative action-budget state, replacing the actions-left counter
Semantic drift: place feature values on a similarity graph so drift favours near neighbours
tasks.notes: Sky to Storm should be likelier than Sky to Sea. This also lets the scholars reconstruct a plausible intermediate rather than only a right or wrong value.

tasks.description: Prestige asymmetry: borrowing flows down the prestige gradient rather than symmetrically by contact weight
tasks.notes: Creates the areal-feature trap: unrelated neighbours converging because they all copied the same prosperous culture. Depends on condition state because prestige is derived from it.

tasks.description: Second founding stock: seed two unrelated ancestral cultures at game start
tasks.notes: The player still leads a band from one stock and is still scored on recovering that stock's truth; the second exists to contaminate the record.

tasks.description: Substrate inheritance: dying and displaced cultures leave traces in whoever succeeds them
tasks.notes: Needs a second lineage to inherit from, so it follows the second founding stock. Traces may be unrelated traditions or mutated sibling ones.

tasks.description: Taboo and deliberate archaism: sanctify a custom against drift, or revive one already lost
tasks.notes: A second lever beyond Hold, and a systematic bias for the scholars to fall for.

tasks.description: Richer inter-culture relations: trade, conquest and hostility beyond distance-and-terrain contact
Expand the corpus: more customs, more parts per custom, more values per part
tasks.notes: Content work. Soft-linked to semantic drift because new values are best authored once the similarity graph exists to place them on.

milestones.name: Reconstruction
milestones.goal: Make the scholars fallible in ways that reward how the player played, not just what survived.

tasks.description: Chronicle carries the evidence the scholars later consume
tasks.notes: Attestation has to be sourced from something recorded. The chronicle is what the player actually saw happen, which keeps the scoring legible in hindsight.

tasks.description: Uneven attestation derived from in-game events, never from a random roll
tasks.notes: A culture that kept Carved stones, held a long stable period or sat in broad contact leaves more for the scholars. Makes being legible to the future a goal in itself.

tasks.description: Deeper scholar model: weighted evidence, competing hypotheses and sub-grouping rather than flat comparison
Scoring accounts for the second stock: contamination misleads, but the player's own ancestral truth stays the target
tasks.notes: False unity across the two stocks becomes a scoreable error. Soft-linked to the scholar model, which it should reflect but need not wait for.
